title: Downtown St. George's Square redesign and construction plan
subtitle: Also: Memorial Cup bid funding, 343 Waterloo Avenue rezoning, accessible ramps, camera penalties and public appointment policy.
overview: Council approved the first phase of downtown infrastructure renewal, including the Wyndham Street North sequencing and construction mitigation plans. It also approved the St. George's Square concept plan {{vote:m26}}, with changes: a smaller play area, placemaking lighting, a rethink of the Family Fountain basin, and final design returning for approval by the end of 2025. Staff can now adjust patio, parking and encroachment fees during construction.

Council backed the Guelph Storm's 2027 Memorial Cup bid with a conditional grant and in-kind arena support {{vote:m12}}, rezoned 343 Waterloo Avenue for mixed-use housing with an affordable housing agreement {{vote:m4}}, and endorsed a community-led approach to business accessibility, including permanent solutions. Speed camera and red light camera tickets will move to an administrative penalty system around January 1, 2026.

Council also suspended the residency eligibility rule in the Public Appointment Policy while staff review it, and appointed five people to the Accessibility Advisory Committee. After a closed session, the Mayor reported that council received information and gave direction to staff on a downtown land acquisition matter.

decisions.detail: Council approved the concept plan with directions for flexible design, natural heritage materials, a smaller play area, placemaking lighting, a reworked fountain basin and budget reporting {{vote:m26}}.

Council approved the 2025 capital implementation plan, Phase 1 sequencing with extended working hours, the mitigation plan, delegated authority to adjust patio, parking and encroachment fees, and final square design returning for approval by the end of 2025.
Council approved a one-time $600,000 grant and up to $100,000 in Sleeman Centre in-kind costs from the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve, contingent on a successful bid {{vote:m12}}.
Council amended the zoning for the property, requiring a full site plan application, an affordable housing agreement before permits, and payment of applicable fees {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved moving speed camera and red light camera violations to an administrative penalty system around January 1, 2026, with related by-laws and agreements.

Council endorsed a community-led approach to business accessibility, including StopGap-style initiatives and permanent solutions, and encouraged the Downtown Guelph Business Association and Chamber of Commerce to promote them.
Council suspended the eligibility and qualifications section of the policy and directed staff to report back on residency eligibility.

debate: On 343 Waterloo Avenue, several councillors praised the project but questioned the process, saying it bypassed normal planning review and could set a precedent. The Mayor said all public notice rules were followed, two affordable units would be secured, and the timeline could shorten by months.

Staff said planning staff did not attend because technical studies and provincial policy conformity were not yet complete. They said the route adds little overall efficiency but gives the applicant certainty for its federal housing financing application.

On the Memorial Cup, councillors asked about drawing on the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve for a for-profit team, hotel capacity, and downtown construction hurting the city's image. Staff said wayfinding work would likely be deferred and the reserve's smaller funding streams would continue. One councillor opposed it partly over that deferral.

Delegates on accessible ramps said temporary ramps need to come with permanent fixes and landlord responsibility. One delegate wanted the city to explore municipal powers; another wanted city leadership and continuity. Council added permanent solutions, and the Mayor preferred letting the community lead before committing funds.

On St. George's Square, some councillors said the concept lacked cohesion or a standout feature, and opposed the fountain and washroom placement. Others supported it with the amendments. The Mayor said the close vote showed how much the final design matters.
